analysis: Examined docs/developer/test.md base units 1-1019 against the head patch, which only inserts a 'Prompt Preparation And Admission' documentation section at head lines 322-345. It documents PromptTokenCacheTests (synthetic tokenizers via LocalTokenizerLoader with no download, piecewise, cached and cross-turn token-ID equality, and disabling reuse after a background-comparison mismatch), ChatTemplateLoopRewritesTests, InboundChatRequestDecodeTests (merged admission body decode versus separate decoders), ServeLoopColdLoadTests (requests parked on cold loads and fit decisions), PROMPT_TOKEN_CACHE_MODEL_DIRS for local model directories, and a 'darkbloom benchmark --prompt-prep' CPU timing mode. This is documentation only, with no code, config, gate or deployment change in the supplied evidence. It weakens no stated control, including SEC-035/T-041 cache-scope language, T-008 fail-closed encryption, or TB-011 authorization. The text implies new runtime surface outside this batch: a prompt-token cache with cross-turn reuse and a merged inbound admission decoder. If that cache is shared across requests, it could interact with T-041/SEC-035 cross-tenant reuse and timing (A-001), because cacheSalt scoping applies to KV prefixes and nothing here says whether token caches are scoped. The merged decode could also differ from the separate decoders on adversarial bodies (ADV-002 via the coordinator). Integration should verify the corresponding Swift sources (PromptTokenCache, the loop rewrites, the InboundChatRequest decoder and the ServeLoop cold-load path) for scoping, bounds and fail-closed behavior. No source was supplied for them, so no finding is raised here.
